Aging is hard. It’s jarring when the luscious, flowing locks of your youth start to disappear before your very eyes. But it can’t be helped—or can it? Red light therapy has been used to treat inflammation, pain relief, and wrinkles, and it's now being applied to hair regrowth. It’s also a much more accessible option than flying to Istanbul for a full-on hair transplant.
iRestore’s Elite red light therapy cap appeared on my radar because of my own hair woes, including scalp irritation and eczema. My hope was that it could help with cell regeneration and kill off the bacteria causing flares.
However, an even better test subject stood right before me—my husband, who is dealing with a rapidly receding hairline. He’s always excited to help with mattress and sleep product testing, so I roped him into testing this hair-growth helmet—for science, of course. To help understand said science, I also spoke with Zakia Rahman, MD, FAAD . Rahman is a clinical professor of dermatology at Stanford University School of Medicine, and a trailblazer in red light therapy research.
Red light therapy didn’t start as a treatment for anti-aging and recovery. It actually came about as an accidental solution for hair loss in the 1960s , when Hungarian scientist Endre Mester was researching whether exposure to red light could treat cancer in hairless mice. Imagine his surprise when the mice started growing hair!
Red light therapy has come a long way since then. Rahman explained that red light wavelengths activate the mitochondria in skin cells and increase blood flow to hair follicles. This uptick in stimulation encourages mitochondria to increase their production of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), which promotes new growth.
When it comes to efficacy, we noted that iRestore Elite is FDA-cleared . This is a designation bestowed on moderate-risk tools that are sufficiently similar to other cleared devices already on the market. There are specific pathways that devices must follow to obtain FDA clearance, and the iRestore Elite was cleared through the FDA's 510(k) premarket evaluation.
There are three hair-growth devices in iRestore's lineup: the entry-level Essential ($499) , the mid-tier Professional ($899) , and the Elite ($1,899) . Each contains iRestore’s “Lumitech” technology, which combines LED lights and medical-grade lasers. These laser diodes are proprietary to iRestore and are called Vixo lasers, operating in the 655- to 680-nanometer (nm) range. ( Preliminary studies with mice have shown that using red light in the 600- to 660-nm range, and infrared wavelengths in the 800- to 850-nm range, can promote everything from cell regeneration to pain relief.)
The idea is that this dynamic duo can penetrate deeper into the skin than ordinary red light with lasers, while the LEDs ensure light is distributed across the scalp for maximum efficacy. Together, they reach a maximum of 2,500 milliwatts (mW), compared to the Professional's 1,410 mW and Essential's 600 mW.
The Elite is iRestore’s top-of-the-line offering and has the most LEDs of the three laser hair-growth systems, with 500 diodes total—that's 300 lasers and 200 LEDs. The Essential has 51 lasers and 69 LEDs for a total of 120 diodes, while the iRestore Pro has 82 lasers and 200 LEDs for a total of 282 diodes. The Elite was also designed to cover more of the scalp. The Elite requires 12 minutes of daily use, while the Professional and Essential require 25 minutes every other day.
If price is not an object, the Elite is the no-brainer choice for more concentrated light therapy, shorter use time, and potentially faster results.
The helmet arrived in hefty red packaging, containing the helmet, portable battery pack, charging cord, and a red-and-black zippered travel case. It feels very fragile, and I wouldn't throw it around—then again, you probably wouldn't be shoving an $1,899 helmet in the back of your bathroom vanity.
While you’re only wearing the helmet for 12 minutes during your daily session, the red lights do feel like you're sitting under bright, hot sunlight. The remote displays a countdown of how many minutes you have left and beeps when it's done. I was testing the helmet to treat my dry scalp and eczema, and I checked my watch every single minute, feeling warmer and warmer. Sweating is a big no-no for eczema, so I wasn’t thrilled to experience this side effect. With time, my husband was able to get used to this, as it’s not painful, just uncomfortable at first.
Within the first two weeks of continuous use (this does include use of iRestore's shampoo, conditioner, supplements, and serum ), I was thrilled to see baby hairs begin to pop up around his hairline. This continued through the first two months of use. The top of his crown had more volume and overall hair density, while new growth appeared in the more drastically affected areas near his forehead. While it didn’t cover up the scalp altogether, it was enough for old college friends and family members to remark on how good his hair looked.
The effects aren't permanent, though. Unfortunately, my husband fell off the bandwagon and stopped the iRestore routine around the holidays due to travel. The case that comes with the iRestore Elite makes it super portable, but we were nervous about leaving it behind as we hopped from place to place. Just as they had so quickly appeared, stopping the treatments made the progress fade in a matter of weeks. Just like that, he was back to square one.
Rahman likens this phenomenon to the importance of daily diet and exercise—one instance of either won't make a difference in your health or daily routine. Rather, it's the consistent practice that delivers results. When I told her that my husband's hair growth had fallen off , she strongly encouraged us to pick it back up.
One of the biggest claims from iRestore, though, was that consistent use of an iRestore device like the Elite could lead to hair growth within 16 weeks. The star ingredient in the serum and shampoo is plant-based Redensyl, which is meant to fortify hair follicles during their regrowth. Additional elements like the shampoo's castor oil and biotin, vegan keratin, and argan oil in the conditioner also act as natural strengtheners.
The supplements contained natural dihydrotestosterone (DHT) blockers derived from saw palmetto. These blockers work to prevent the enzyme (5-alpha reductase) from transforming testosterone into DHT. In essence, this hormone is the driver behind hair loss, excessive shedding, and general inactivity in hair growth.
The idea is that using these extras alongside the iRestore Elite will help achieve lasting results. I tested the Elite for eczema and dry scalp, but these didn't do much for me. With my husband’s consistent use, they seemed to yield results a bit faster. (Full disclosure: He was also using his usual Rogaine throughout this entire process.) The supplements, strengthening serum, shampoo, and conditioner are included with the purchase of the iRestore Elite; we figured adding them into his routine could only help. It's convenient that these are included, but you don't need to go out of your way to buy them specifically from iRestore.
There are plenty of anti-hair-loss treatments available, from visiting your dermatologist to establish a hair health regimen to oral and topical medications to hair transplant procedures. All have their merits in slowing hair thinning and promoting fuller hair. I asked Rahman whether red light therapy could be its own treatment or was best used with the extras. “Combination therapy will work better than a stand-alone," she says. Red light therapy can operate on its own, but the benefits only increase when you throw in minoxidil and other proven hair-loss measures.
The iRestore Elite did quell my scalp flare-ups, but I don't think I'd throw down almost two grand for that. But when it comes to hair regrowth, that's a totally different story. My husband was already using Rogaine before the iRestore Elite sho…

Senegal have been confirmed as winners of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations after the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) overturned a ruling that had stripped them of the title and handed it to hosts Morocco.
The court, based in Lausanne, Switzerland, upheld an appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against a decision by the Confederation of African Football's (CAF) appeal board. The board had declared that Senegal forfeited the final and recorded Morocco as 3-0 winners. The original 1-0 result in Senegal's favour now stands.
"By blowing his whistle to restart play, the Referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met - both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume," the court said.
"In the Panel's view, there is no doubt that the effects of the Referee's decision were limited to the pitch. As such, the Panel considers that the Referee's decision was covered by the 'field of play' doctrine."
Under the doctrine, CAS does not review decisions taken on the pitch by referees unless the rules were applied arbitrarily or in bad faith.
"The Panel acknowledged that the Referee had to make a decision in an atmosphere of extreme tension. However, these circumstances do not justify describing the decision as 'arbitrary'," CAS added.
The Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF) said it would "pursue all necessary legal avenues" to contest the ruling.
The FRMF said it objected to the rejection of its request to postpone the decision. It added that it could take the case to Switzerland's Federal Supreme Court, which rules on procedural matters rather than the merits of a case.
In a statement, the FRMF referred to what it said was "contact" between Ulrich Haas, a German arbitrator who was one of the three CAS panel members, and the president of the FSF 48 hours before the decision was announced.
The final was played on 18 January at the Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium in Rabat, Morocco. The score was 0-0 deep into stoppage time when the Congolese referee, Jean-Jacques Ngambo Ndala, awarded Morocco a penalty after a VAR review.
Senegal's players, led by coach Pape Thiaw, walked off the pitch in protest for 15 minutes, and fans tried to storm the field.
When play resumed, Brahim Díaz's penalty was saved by Senegal goalkeeper Édouard Mendy. Pape Gueye then scored in extra time to win the match for Senegal.
CAF's disciplinary board first fined and banned players and officials from both Senegal and Morocco, with fines totalling more than $1 million, but it left the result unchanged.
Morocco appealed. In March, CAF's appeal board ruled that Senegal's conduct fell under Articles 82 and 84 of the tournament regulations, declared that they had forfeited the final, and awarded Morocco their first African title since 1976.
The FSF lodged its appeal with CAS on 25 March. Morocco's football federation argued that the referee's decision was not protected by the "field of play" doctrine, that by leaving the pitch Senegal had breached Articles 82 and 84, and that the referee should have ended the match early.
The panel rejected those arguments. It found that the two articles apply only when a team's conduct leads a referee to abandon a match permanently, so they did not apply in this case. A hearing was held behind closed doors in Lausanne on 8 October.
CAS noted that the FSF, Thiaw and some players had already been sanctioned by CAF in separate disciplinary proceedings.

A funeral was held earlier in southern Gaza for three Palestinians killed in an Israeli strike
At least seven Palestinians, including a senior Hamas security official, have been killed in Israeli air strikes in the Gaza Strip, health officials and first responders say.
Naeem Abu Nahel, the head of Hamas's internal security service, was targeted in western Gaza City, Gaza's Hamas-run interior ministry said. The 50-year-old had only been in the position since September, when his predecessor was captured in a raid by Israeli special forces .
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defence Minister Israel Katz announced that Abu Nahel was "eliminated" by the Israeli military.
The six other people were killed in two earlier air strikes elsewhere in Gaza.
Three people, including a teenage boy, were killed in the Wadi Gaza area, south of Gaza City, according to the health officials and first responders. The other three were killed at a police station in the al-Mawasi area, west of Khan Younis, they added.
Gaza's police force, which operates under the interior ministry, said two of its officers were among those who died in the second attack. It also accused Israel of "an ongoing campaign targeting the police apparatus aimed at sowing chaos" in the territory.
The Israeli military said it struck "military operatives" in both areas.
Witnesses said an Israeli drone targeted Naeem Abu Nahel as he was walking on a side street near a tent camp for displaced people in Gaza City.
Several other people were reportedly seriously injured in the strike.
The Israeli military said Abu Nahel had "possessed extensive institutional knowledge" about Hamas's internal security service - which is responsible for enforcing discipline, protecting infrastructure and rooting out informants - and that his death constituted "a blow to the apparatus's management capabilities".
It also alleged that he had advanced attacks on Israeli troops and civilians during the war and that it killed him "to remove the threat he posed".
Gaza's interior ministry said Abu Nahel's killing followed what it described as the internal security service's "important achievements in combating gangs collaborating with the occupation [Israel] and operating in areas under the control of its military".
Gaza's health ministry warned that there was a rapid rise in cases of meningitis in October
Violence has continued in Gaza since Israel and Hamas agreed to a US-brokered ceasefire in October last year. Israeli strikes take place almost daily in areas under Hamas's control, which are home to 2.1 million people, most of them displaced.
At least 1,679 people have been killed in Gaza over the past 13 months, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.
Israel says six of its soldiers have been killed in Gaza during the same period.
The humanitarian situation also remains dire, with heavy rainfall earlier this month causing flooding and damage to thousands of shelters for displaced families.
The UN and its partners have called on Israel - which controls Gaza's crossings - to allow in more supplies to help Palestinians prepare for the winter, including tents, heaters and water pumps, as well as vaccines and medicines to combat infectious diseases.
On Tuesday, the health ministry warned that there had been a rapid rise in cases of meningitis, with 272 reported in October - about eight times the usual monthly average.
Fifteen deaths had been attributed to the infection so far this year, including five reported between August and October, it said.
Israeli military body Cogat said on Monday it was "working to provide a dedicated humanitarian response" and that a newly approved package of pumps, generators, water tankers and medical equipment had been presented at a meeting with UN agencies.
The Gaza war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage.
Since then, more than 74,740 people have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza, the health ministry says.

The Court of Arbitration for Sport on Tuesday unanimously ruled in favour of Senegal in the appeal to reclaim the Africa Cup of Nations title, 10 months after a chaotic final against Morocco. Senegal won the match in January but was stripped of the title in March because many of the team's players had walked off the pitch in protest over a penalty given to the opposing side. Morocco said it would contest the ruling.
Senegal on Tuesday regained their Africa Cup of Nations title after winning an appeal at the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) against the decision by the Confederation of African Football to declare Morocco the winners following a chaotic final in January.
CAS said in a statement it had "upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF)" by a "unanimous decision".
As a result, Senegal's original 1-0 victory after extra time is reinstated and they are confirmed as African champions for the second time following their triumph in 2022.
Watch more AFCON 2025: CAS set to hand down ruling on controversial final
In March, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) sensationally overturned the result of the final, awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory, and the title, after many Senegalese players walked off the pitch in protest at a penalty given to the hosts with the game still goalless.
The CAF Appeals Committee had justified its decision to overturn the result and declare Morocco champions based on Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations.
Those state that if a team "refuses to play or leaves the ground before the regular end of the match without the authorisation of the referee, it shall be considered (loser) and shall be eliminated for good from the current competition".
However, the Senegal players eventually returned to the pitch and the final carried on.
Watch more AFCON 2025: Morocco's dream ends as Senegal earn second title in five years
The three-person CAS panel therefore considered the referee's decision to restart the final showed "the conditions for resuming the match had been met", and that articles 82 and 84 were therefore "not applicable in this case".
"This is a huge decision because it is the first time that we have had to rule on the fate of a continental final," said Matthieu Reeb, the director general of the Swiss-based sports court.
Senegal star Sadio Mané said the court's decision "fills us with joy", while the Senegalese Football Federation president Abdoulaye Fall said the ruling "does justice to sport".
On Instagram, Mané sent his "respect and encouragement to the Moroccan people and Morocco players. They had a great run and can be proud of that... the Senegalese and Moroccan people are brothers. Let's hope our passion for football continues to bring us together".
However, the Moroccan federation reacted by promising to "pursue all necessary legal avenues" to contest the CAS ruling.
It a statement, it referred to what it said was "contact" between German arbitrator Ulrich Haas, one of the three CAS panel members who issued the ruling, and the president of the Senegalese Football Federation 48 hours before the decision was announced.
The AFCON final in Rabat was goalless late in normal time, and heading to extra time, when hosts Morocco were awarded a controversial penalty.
The decision by Congolese referee Jean-Jacques Ndala to point to the spot after a VAR check when Brahim Diaz went down under a challenge in the box infuriated Senegal players and supporters in the ground.
That lit the fuse for the chaos which ensued, as most of the Senegal team walked off the field of play, while away fans fought with security personnel and tried to enter the pitch.
However, the Senegal players eventually came back on and the game restarted after a long delay, only for Diaz to fluff his kick which was saved.
The match was eventually decided by Pape Gueye's goal in extra time, and the Senegal players were celebrated as heroes on their return to Dakar.
The Lions of Teranga also paraded with the trophy before a friendly match at the Stade de France in Paris , two weeks after the CAF ruling which stripped them of their crown.
The Senegalese federation had denounced the ruling as the "most blatant administrative robbery in the history of our sport".
Morocco, who went on to reach the quarter-finals of this year's World Cup in North America , have therefore still only ever won one AFCON title, in 1976.
Read more AFCON 2027 qualifiers: Senegal and five other nations secure spot
Both nations last week secured qualification for the next Cup of Nations, which will take place in Kenya , Tanzania and Uganda next June and July.

Israeli airstrikes in the Gaza Strip killed seven people on Tuesday, including Hamas's director of internal security, according to Palestinian officials, despite a ceasefire that has been in place since October 2025.
Gaza's interior ministry, which operates under Hamas authority, said an airstrike in Gaza City killed Brigadier General Naeem Abu Nahal, director-general of the Internal Security Service.
Israel's military said it had "struck a senior terrorist" from Hamas.
Mahmoud Bassal, spokesman for Gaza's civil defence agency, said several other people were in critical condition after the same strike in Gaza City's Rimal neighbourhood.
Bassal said three people, including a 17-year-old, had been killed earlier on Tuesday in a separate Israeli airstrike near Gaza City.
Three more were killed in a third strike, on a police station in the Al-Mawasi area of southern Gaza, he added.
Gaza's police force, which also operates under Hamas, said two policemen aged 23 and 33 were among the dead. It condemned the strike as "part of an ongoing campaign targeting the police apparatus".
Israel's military said it had "struck terrorists in the area" of the police station, but did not confirm the strike that is believed to have killed the 17-year-old.
Israel and Hamas regularly accuse each other of violating the ceasefire, which came into effect after two years of war triggered by the Hamas-led attack on Israel on 7 October 2023.
More than 1,650 Palestinians have been killed since the truce began, according to a tally based on data from Gaza's health ministry, which also operates under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.
Over the same period, the Israeli military says seven of its soldiers and one civilian contractor have been killed.
Most of Gaza's 2.1 million people are displaced and living in tents or makeshift shelters. Israel's military says it controls more than 60% of the territory.
The strikes come as talks continue in Israel to form a new government after legislative elections in October produced no clear winner.
The centrist Gadi Eisenkot is seeking to build a coalition that would end the long tenure of Benjamin Netanyahu, who is now caretaker prime minister.
But Netanyahu, who has staked his reputation on ensuring Israel's security since the 7 October attack, remains in charge of military operations while negotiations go on.

"Aile içi şiddet" raporunda 2025 yılında aile içi şiddete maruz kalanların sayısının 280 bin 129'a çıkarak rekor seviyeye ulaştığına işaret edilerek, bu sayının 272 bin 495 olduğu 2024'e göre yüzde 2,8 oranında arttığı belirtildi.
2025'te 197 bin 667 kadın ve kız çocuğunun aile içi şiddete uğradığı bilgisi paylaşılan raporda, kadın ve kızların aile içi şiddete maruz kalanların toplamı içindeki payının yüzde 70,6 olduğu ifade edildi.
Haftada 4 kadın ve kız çocuğunun aile içi şiddet nedeniyle hayatını kaybettiğine işaret edilen raporda, geçen yıl 209'u kadın ve kız çocuğu olmak üzere 292 kişinin aile içi şiddet sonucu öldüğü kaydedildi.
Raporda hayatını kaybeden kadınların 130'unun eşi veya eski eşi tarafından öldürüldüğü, eşi veya eski eşi tarafından öldürülen erkeklerin sayısının da 23 olduğu aktarıldı.
"Kadınlara yönelik cinsiyete dayalı suçlar" raporunda 2025'te ülkede toplam 342 kadın ve kız çocuğunun şiddet eylemi sonucunda öldüğü ifade edildi. Bu sayı 2024'te 308 olarak kayıtlara geçmişti.
Cinsel suçlara maruz kalan kadın ve kızların sayısının 2024'e göre yüzde 2,3 artarak 2025'te 54 bin 675’e yükseldiği vurgulanan raporda, cinsel suç mağdurlarının yüzde 49,5'inin 18 yaşın altında olduğu kaydedildi.
Raporda, çevrim içi ortamda 31 bin 221 kadın ve kız çocuğunun "dijital şiddet" mağduru olduğu, bu sayının da 2024'e göre yüzde 15,1 oranında arttığı ifade edildi.
İçişleri Bakanı Alexander Dobrindt, bu rakamların şok edici olduğunu belirterek, "Tüm alanlarda mağdur sayılarında artış gözlemliyoruz." dedi.
Dobrindt, 2021'den bu yana aile içi şiddet mağdur sayısının her yıl arttığını kaydetti.
Mağdurların özellikle kadın ve kız çocukları olduğunu vurgulayan Dobrindt, şüphelilerin yüzde 75'inin erkek olduğunu belirtti.
Aile içi şiddete uğrayanların yüzde 31'den fazlasının yabancı, yüzde 68,7'sinin Alman vatandaşı olduğunu aktaran Dobrindt, tüm bu sayıların ardında en acı verici anılar ve uzun süren etkilerin bulunduğunu söyledi.
Dobrindt, aile içi şiddete karşı önlemlerin alınmasının siyasetin gündeminde olduğunu ifade etti.
Eğitim, Aile, Yaşlılar, Kadın ve Gençlik Bakanı Prien de burada paylaşılan sayıların sadece polise bildirilen vakaları kapsadığını, araştırmaların şiddet eylemlerinin çoğunun polise bildirilmediğini ortaya koyduğunu vurguladı.
Prien, toplumda bu tür olayların konuşulması gerektiğini dile getirdi.
Bu nedenle özellikle daha okul çağında başlayan önleyici çalışmalara önem verilmesi gerektiğinin altını çizen Prien, "İnsanların, özellikle de erkeklerin zihninde bir değişim gerçekleşmesini sağlamalıyız." dedi.

Tasarım platformu Canva, yapay zeka ajanlarının ve geliştiricilerin şirketin tasarım araçlarından yararlanmasını sağlayan Canva MCP altyapısını genel kullanıma açtığını duyurdu. Şirket, yenilenen altyapısıyla birlikte yeni API'ler, genişletilmiş komut satırı araçları ve yapay zeka destekli tasarım özelliklerini kullanıma sundu. Böylece geliştiriciler, Canva'nın tasarım teknolojilerini kendi uygulamalarına ve otomatik iş akışlarına entegre edebilecek.
Canva'nın Model Context Protocol (MCP) altyapısı, yapay zeka asistanlarının Canva'nın araçlarına bağlanarak tasarım oluşturmasını ve mevcut tasarımlar üzerinde işlem yapmasını sağlıyor. Şirketin açıklamasına göre bu altyapı halihazırda ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini ve Muse gibi yapay zeka asistanlarında milyonlarca tasarım işlemini destekliyor.
Daha önce Canva MCP'ye erişim, belirli geliştiriciler ve şirketin iş ortaklarıyla sınırlıydı . Yeni güncellemeyle birlikte bekleme listesi kaldırıldı. Geliştiriciler artık Canva Developer Portal üzerinden kayıt olarak MCP bağlantılarını oluşturabiliyor.
Yenilenen Canva MCP ile yapay zeka ajanları, kullanıcıların verdiği komutlar doğrultusunda düzenlenebilir tasarımlar, görseller ve videolar oluşturabiliyor. Ayrıca görsellerin arka planını kaldırabiliyor, mevcut görselleri düzenlenebilir katmanlara dönüştürebiliyor, tasarımların boyutlarını değiştirebiliyor ve tamamlanan çalışmaları farklı dosya biçimlerinde dışa aktarabiliyor.
Örneğin bir kullanıcı, yapay zeka asistanından yeni bir ürün için tanıtım kampanyası hazırlamasını istediğinde asistan, Canva'nın araçlarını kullanarak sosyal medya görselleri ve sunumlar oluşturabiliyor. Hazırlanan tasarımlar daha sonra Canva üzerinden düzenlenebiliyor.
Şirket, yeni sürümde yapay zeka ajanlarının araçları daha kolay kullanabilmesi için MCP altyapısını da yeniden düzenledi. Benzer işlevlere sahip araçlar bir araya getirilirken ajanların hangi işlemi hangi araçla gerçekleştireceğini belirlemesi kolaylaştırıldı. Bu sayede daha küçük yapay zeka modelleriyle çalışan ajanların da Canva araçlarından daha verimli yararlanması hedefleniyor.
Canva ayrıca kendi geliştirdiği görsel üretim modeli Canva Craft 'ı da MCP ve API aracılığıyla dışarıdan erişime açtı. Bu kapsamda geliştiriciler, Canva Craft'ın görsel üretim özelliklerini doğrudan kendi ürünlerinde kullanabilecek.
Canva, geliştiricilere tasarım araçlarına erişmek için üç farklı yöntem sunuyor. Bunlardan ilki olan MCP, yapay zeka ajanlarının kullanıcı komutlarını yorumlayarak uygun Canva araçlarını kullanmasını sağlıyor. İkinci yöntem olan REST API'leri ise geliştiricilerin tasarım oluşturma, görsel üretme, arka plan kaldırma ve Magic Layers gibi özellikleri doğrudan kendi uygulamalarına eklemesine olanak tanıyor.
Üçüncü seçenek olan Canva CLI, özellikle yazılım geliştiren yapay zeka ajanlarının ve çok sayıda işlemi otomatik gerçekleştirmek isteyen ekiplerin kullanımına yönelik. Şirketin paylaştığı verilere göre ekim ayında Canva CLI üzerinden girilen komutların yüzde 72'si yapay zeka ajanlarından geldi.
Canva, yeni hizmet hesapları ve API üzerinden ücretlendirme desteğiyle işletmelerin çalışanların kişisel hesaplarına bağlı kalmadan otomatik iş akışları oluşturabilmesini de sağlıyor. Bu yöntemle geliştiriciler, müşterilerinin ayrı ayrı Canva hesabı açmasına gerek kalmadan Canva özelliklerini kendi ürünleri içinde sunabilecek.
Canva'nın paylaştığı verilere göre ekim ayından bu yana yaklaşık 500 bin kişi, MCP bağlantıları üzerinden Canva'ya kaydoldu. Canva MCP'nin kullanımı ise ekim ayında bir önceki aya kıyasla yüzde 93 arttı. Şirket ayrıca yapay zeka asistanları üzerinden Canva'ya gelen kullanıcıların Canva'nın yapay zeka özelliklerini kullanma olasılığının diğer kullanıcılara göre 2,5 kat daha yüksek olduğunu belirtiyor. Bu kanaldan beklenen yıllık tekrarlayan gelir de eylül ve ekim ayları arasında yüzde 300'ün üzerinde artış gösterdi. Ancak şirket, söz konusu gelirin tutarını paylaşmadı.
Kasım ayının başlarında çalışanlarının yüzde 22'sini kapsayan bir yeniden yapılanma ile karşımıza çıkan Canva, bu yeni yaklaşımı ile tasarım araçlarını farklı uygulamaların ve yapay zeka ajanlarının kullanabildiği bir altyapıya dönüştürerek dijital ürünlerin tasarım süreçlerinde daha fazla yer almayı amaçlıyor.

The Court of Arbitration for Sport has ruled Senegal to be the winners of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations, which concluded in January; Senegal beat Morocco 1-0 in the final but were stripped of the title in March, which led to their appeal
The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) has announced Senegal as the winners of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON).
In response, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation said it was 'astonished' by the decision and 'affirms its intention to pursue all available legal procedures to appeal the decision'.
Senegal beat Morocco 1-0 in the final in January but were stripped of the title by a Confederation of African Football (CAF) appeal board in March for breaking competition rules by walking off the pitch because of a late disallowed goal and a controversial penalty awarded to their opponents.
Senegal's protest caused a delay of over 15 minutes and when their players returned to the pitch, Morocco's Brahim Diaz missed the penalty to force the match into extra time, with Pape Gueye going on to score the winner.
"The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) has upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF) concerning the final of the Africa Cup of Nations Morocco 2025 (AFCON 2025)," a CAS statement read.
"The decision rendered by the CAF appeal board is set aside and the decision by the CAF disciplinary board is reinstated. Consequently, the result obtained at the end of the AFCON 2025 final is confirmed (1-0 for Senegal)."
Morocco's appeal was initially rejected but a CAF panel did uphold it and found Senegal's walk-off meant they had forfeited the match, awarding a 3-0 win to Morocco.
CAF said Senegal infringed on article 82 of AFCON's regulations, which states if a team refuses to play or leaves the ground before the end of regulation time without the referee's authorisation, it will be considered the loser and eliminated from the competition.
Article 84 states any team that violates article 82 will be permanently eliminated and lose the match 3-0.
However, the IFAB laws of the game state: "The decisions of the referee regarding facts connected with play, including whether or not a goal is scored and the result of the match, are final."
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Senegal appealed to CAS, calling the decision "a travesty", and have now been reinstated as champions.
The Moroccan federation wrote to the CAS earlier on Tuesday asking them to postpone the announcement of their decision. They wanted CAS to investigate allegations that one of the members of the CAS panel - Ulrich Haas - spoke on the telephone to the president of the Senegal FA Abdoulaye Fall on Sunday.
CAS confirmed it had received a challenge petition 'a few minutes' before the announcement but decided 'there were insufficient grounds at this stage to postpone the notification of the award'.
In April, IFAB - who are football's law makers - introduced a law stating that any players who leave the field of play in protest at a referee's decision can be sent off. The adoption of this law is at the discretion of the competition organiser.
"Common sense has prevailed because the Court of Arbitration for Sport have effectively confirmed that Senegal did win the 2025 AFCON.
"Morocco were very unhappy because they felt that the rules of the tournament had been broken by Senegal when they left the pitch. They felt that at that stage Senegal should have forfeited the game.
"They went to the African Confederation Appeal Board and there was an appeal hearing in March. That appeal decided that yes, Morocco were right and they should be the winners and the result of the game was changed from a 1-0 win to Senegal to a 3-0 win to Morocco.
"Then we had the next chapter in this story because Senegal were also very unhappy with the decision of the appeal board, so they went to CAS in Switzerland. There was a hearing in October and now we have had the decision - a unanimous decision from the three judges.
"I don't want to tempt fate, because let's wait and see what the Moroccan Federation say, but what I would say to you is that they have fought this all the way, they believe that this is an injustice and they are one of the most powerful football associations in Africa.
"They are co-hosts of the next World Cup in 2030 and they have a very close relationships with the leadership at FIFA.
"I'm not suggesting that anything untoward is going on, but they still do have options. For instance, if they feel there has been something wrong in the procedures at the CAS hearing, they could go to the Swiss Federal Tribunal.
"I think the Moroccan Federation, according to what Reuters are reporting this afternoon, are unhappy with the way CAS handled this appeal and they have complained to CAS because they believe that one of the judges actually spoke on the phone to the president of the Senegal Federation on Sunday afternoon, so perhaps that is an avenue that they are going to explore."
The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) has upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF, in French) concerning the final of the Africa Cup of Nations Morocco 2025 (AFCON 2025).
The decision rendered by the CAF Appeal Board is set aside and the decision by the CAF Disciplinary Board is reinstated. Consequently, the result obtained at the end of the AFCON 2025 final is confirmed (1-0 for Senegal).
The FSF appealed to CAS against a decision of the CAF Appeal Board declaring that the Senegal national team forfeited the AFCON 2025 final and recording the Moroccan national team as the winners.
In their appeal, the FSF argued that the decision of the Referee, Mr Jean-Jacques Ngambo Ndala, to resume the match at the 109th minute (90+19) during the AFCON 2025 final and to allow it to be concluded with a sporting result could not be reviewed, pursuant to the 'field of play' doctrine.
The FRMF argued, on the contrary, that the Referee's decision did not fall under the 'field of play' doctrine, as it cannot be applicable to the disciplinary consequences of the Senegalese team's behaviour. The FRMF alleged that, by leaving the pitch temporarily, the Senegalese team breached Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations, which should have led the Referee to bring the match to an early conclusion. The FRMF also argued that the Referee erred in law and that his decision was arbitrary.
After having examined the arguments raised by the Parties, the Arbitral Panel considered that the Referee's decision to resume the match or to stop it fell definitively within his sole authority. By blowing his whistle to restart play, the Referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met - both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume.
In the Panel's view, there is no doubt that the effects of the Referee's decision were limited to the pitch. As such, the Panel considers that the Referee's decision was covered by the 'field of play' doctrine. Since Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations are intended solely to determine the outcome of a match when a team's conduct leads the referee to call off the game permanently, they are therefore not applicable in this case. In conclusion, the Panel considers that in resuming the match, the Referee did not err in law.
The Panel acknowledged that the Referee had to make a decision in an atmosphere of extreme tension. However, these circumstances do not justify describing the decision as "arbitrary". On the contrary, the Referee's judgment did not appear to have been affected by factors external to the game.

Police say group seized store in city of Cartagena and local media showed footage of snipers on nearby buildings
A group of armed men with their faces covered seized a supermarket in the Colombian city of Cartagena on Tuesday and are holding 25 people hostage, the president, Abelardo de la Espriella, said on Tuesday.
De la Espriella, said the men were “common criminals” who fled into the supermarket after a failed attempt to hold up an armored truck.
Military and police forces have been deployed to the hostage site, Colombian police said.
Footage shared on social media showed dozens of people rushing out of the Exito supermarket in Cartagena’s La Castellana neighborhood, while local media have shown footage of snipers on nearby buildings in what appears to be a standoff between the armed men and police.
“Thirty people were kidnapped, five ​of whom have already been released. They are older women,” said de la Espriella from the city of ​Villavicencio, where he traveled after an overnight bombing ​there.
Cartagena is one of Colombia’s main tourist destinations. The city of a million people is famous for its well-preserved 18th-century architecture, and the thick stone walls built to defend it from pirate attacks.
The Rafael Núñez airport in Cartagena temporarily suspended its operations on Tuesday after the incident, as the armed forces used one of the runways in ​connection with ​the incident. It later said operations were slowly returning to normal and landings were reopened about 45 minutes after the suspension.
Local media reported the hostages are ​being her at the Castellana location of ​the ⁠Éxito supermarket chain.

In recent days, Ukraine has sunk a Russian warship docked in port in Libya, and Russian missiles have landed in Poland. The Kremlin has not commented on the missiles.
MICHEL MARTIN, HOST: Depending on your point of view, Russia's war in Ukraine is either revving up or winding down. STEVE INSKEEP, HOST: This month, the Trump administration claimed it was making progress toward a negotiated peace. Also this month, the fighting has expanded geographically into Eastern Europe, Northern Europe, even the Mediterranean, as if it was a world war. MARTIN: Joining us to talk about both these dynamics is NPR's Charles Maynes from Moscow. Charles, good morning. CHARLES MAYNES, BYLINE: Morning, Michel. MARTIN: So Russia and Ukraine are both striking out far beyond their borders. How concerned should we be? MAYNES: You know, there have been long concerns that an incident along NATO's northeastern flank near a border in Russia could serve as a tripwire for turning the war in Ukraine into a wider conflict. But recent events have brought that back to our attention. Last week we saw three Russian cruise missiles land in southeastern Poland, and on Saturday, a sanctioned Russian cargo ship was hit by what is presumed to have been a Ukrainian drone in the Baltic Sea. But now we're also seeing action further afield. Ukraine destroyed a Russian naval warship docked in Libya in the Mediterranean. Russia has its own shadow role providing intel to Iran in its war with the U.S. And just this morning, South Korea said it scrambled jets to chase away Russian sorties operating near its airspace. So the spillover is real, and the map is wide. MARTIN: So what is being done to contain it? MAYNES: Well, you know, Russian President Vladimir Putin constantly dismisses this idea that he's seeking direct confrontation with NATO. He says it's absurd. But there have been a spate of recent incidents of bomb threats, cyberattacks, sabotage that some in Europe believe are the work of Russia's security services. Russia's goal, it seems, would be to tear at the alliance's core commitment to collective security - this idea that an attack on one is an attack on all - and it's divided NATO. How do you respond to acts that fall below this threshold of outright war? So for example, President Trump has dismissed incursions by Russia into NATO airspace as basically mistakes. Now, as to other areas where we've seen Ukraine launch attacks, like Libya or apparently the Baltic Sea, it seems to show that Ukraine is intent on striking symbols of Russian power anywhere, and that also makes some supporters of Kyiv nervous. MARTIN: On the diplomatic front, President Trump is suggesting that a peace deal may be in the offing. Why does he say that? MAYNES: Well, after two years, we saw the Trump administration really make no headway. They've changed tactics by expanding the talks beyond Russia and Ukraine to focus on European security as a whole. And the conversations are now fundamentally centered on what security guarantees are on offer to Ukraine, to Russia, and to Europe. But the problem seems to be there's a bit of a disconnect between what that means to each of them. For example, Trump's envoys say Russia is, quote, "comfortable" with NATO-like guarantees for Ukraine. Russian officials have pushed back against that idea hard. But President Trump - he says this is all public posturing, that everyone is being much more flexible behind the scenes. We'll just have to see if he's right. MARTIN: And meanwhile, the war continues. MAYNES: It does, and it was staggering losses, particularly from the Russian side, if new findings published yesterday by various independent Russian media in exile is correct. They've been sifting through data that was hacked from Russia's statistics agency and concluded that upwards of an astonishing 700,000 Russian troops have been killed in this war, and those numbers continue to grow. MARTIN: That is NPR's Charles Maynes in Moscow. Charles, thank you. MAYNES: Thank you.

Watch: India's government is 'scared', cockroach movement leader says after travel ban
One of the leaders of India's "cockroach" movement has said the Delhi government has "completely lost the plot" after he was stopped from leaving the country for the UK.
Saurav Das said he was meant to board a flight on Tuesday morning but was told by immigration officers his passport had been "flagged" because of discrepancies involving his date of birth.
In an interview with the BBC, Das said there were no discrepancies in his documents, accusing the Indian government of using cheap tactics to stop activists from travelling and speaking on issues that matter to young people.
The BBC has reached out to the federal home ministry, Delhi police and airport officials for comment.
Saurav told the BBC World Service's Newshour programme the incident showed the government was "scared".
"They are scared of the cockroach movement. They're scared of young people asking them questions because they have never had to deal with a generation that wants to ask questions so head on. So that jitters them."
By not allowing him to travel, he said the government had lowered India's stature in the world.
"It's international news that I am unable to travel to the UK," he said. "And this shows Prime Minister Modi in such poor light.
"It's a way to harass, to target activists, young voices in India by the Modi government."
Das said he had been invited by the Oxford Union, as well as universities including Cambridge and Edinburgh, to speak about the movement.
Ratna Singh, another leader of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), wrote: "The manner in which Saurav was not allowed to board today raises deeply troubling questions about the state of freedom of expression and the space being allowed for young voices in this country."
On Tuesday, the London School of Economics Student Union's Amnesty International Unit, a student-led charity group, shared a post on Instagram saying that an event featuring Das had been "indefinitely postponed".
Saurav Das (L) speaking following the resignation of India's education minister in July
Das, a former journalist, became one of the faces of the CJP - a Gen Z-led movement that began as satire but has since emerged as a youth-led pressure group.
In July, protests spearheaded by the CJP over exam paper leaks led to the resignation of India's Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan .
In October, CJP leaders including Das were among thousands detained by the police for trying to hold protests demanding the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls. Kumar and the Election Commission have denied wrongdoing.
The same month, Das and Ashutosh Ranka, another CJP leader, were jailed for seven days after being arrested for trespassing at a banned protest site in Delhi.
Das insisted the CJP would continue protesting, but it did not want to be a political party "as of today".
"It's a long haul. We are not here for a short time. We are looking at India in the next 10 to 20 years. How do we develop India into a better country? That is the vision that we want to carry forward."
Abhijeet Dipke, the founder of CJP, wrote on X that if Das "had looted a bank or committed financial fraud", he may have been allowed to fly to London, referring to billionaire bank-loan defaulters who have left India.
There have been other instances in recent years of people being prevented from boarding flights.
In September 2025, Bhanu Tatak, an environmental and anti-dam activist from India's north-eastern Arunachal Pradesh state, was stopped from boarding a flight to Dublin.
In March 2022, Rana Ayyub, an investigative journalist and outspoken critic of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government, was also stopped from boarding a flight to London at the Mumbai airport. She was due to speak at different events on media freedom and the targeting of journalists.
After a summer win, India's Gen Z protesters face a winter of uncertainty

Saurav Das was due to give talks at UK universities on protest movement but says ‘coward government’ prevented him flying
A leader of India’s youth-led Cockroach movement has said he was prevented from leaving Delhi to fly to the UK to give talks on the viral group’s protests.
Saurav Das, 27, has been at the forefront of the Cockroach Janta party (CJP), which has amassed millions of social media followers since its launch in May . Das, who was due to fly out early on Tuesday, said immigration officials told him at the airport that his passport had been flagged.
The incident comes a month after he was detained for defying a security crackdown in Delhi during protests demanding the resignation of India’s chief election commissioner.
“This coward government did not allow me to board my flight to London where I was invited by prestigious universities like Oxford, Cambridge, LSE (London School of Economics), Edinburgh to deliver talks on the Cockroach movement,” Das said in a social media post late on Monday. “Indian students put their heart and soul to organise the events but this anti-intellectual government was scared of me going to these prestigious institutions.”
Das was due to speak at the Oxford Union society on 1 December.
CJP-organised protests in July over alleged examination irregularities forced the education minister to resign , marking a rare climbdown by the government of Narendra Modi.
Critics say human rights and press freedoms have declined since Modi came to power in 2014. Earlier this month, India barred more than 100 foreign speakers from attending a democracy summit organised by the opposition Congress party. Those denied visas included a Norwegian journalist who had previously questioned Modi about press freedom.
In 2022, authorities prevented Sanna Irshad Mattoo, an award-winning photographer from India-administered Kashmir, from flying to the US to collect her Pulitzer prize.

At least 24 people were injured after a car bomb exploded in Villavicencio in central Colombia on Monday, authorities said.
The blast damaged a regional government headquarters as well as neighbouring buildings.
Video footage circulating on social media shows piles of rubble alongside wrecked vehicles and a large crater in the road.
The attack, which has so far not been claimed by any group, comes amid a wave of violence in the South American nation.
Alexander Baquero, the mayor of Villavicencio, has since imposed a temporary ban on motorcycle traffic along several key roads in the city, which is the capital of the Meta Department.
The Colombian army's Seventh Brigade has also been deployed to the area.
Both the mayor's office and the regional government are offering up to 150 million Colombian pesos (around €38,000) for information leading to those responsible.
Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella arrived in Villavicencio at around 9 am local time on Tuesday as he prepared to hold a security meeting and visit the scene of the blast.
"Narcoterrorism is desperate because we are confronting it resolutely," de la Espriella wrote in a post on social media. "It seeks to intimidate us and force us to back down in order to pursue another false peace process."
In a later update, he added that he would "not back down or negotiate with criminals."
"I will confront them with absolute determination and use every tool granted to me by the Constitution and the law to restore security," he wrote on X.

Nicolas Sarkozy and his wife Carla Bruni-Sarkozy are to face trial next year over charges stemming from the former French president's conviction for conspiring to fund his election campaign with money from late Libyan dictator Muammar Gaddafi.
The charges centre on the retraction of the testimony of a key witness who had initially said he had evidence that could incriminate Sarkozy.
Sarkozy was given a five-year sentence in the case last September and became the first French ex-president to go to jail, even though he only spent 20 days behind bars. He has always denied doing anything wrong in the case and the appeals verdict is expected next Monday.
Since losing his re-election bid in 2012, Sarkozy has faced several criminal investigations.
In 2024, he was handed a one-year sentence – of which six months were suspended – over the illegal financing of his 2012 re-election campaign.
In 2021, he was found guilty of trying to bribe a judge and sentenced to three years in jail – two of them suspended – and thus became the first former French president to get a custodial sentence. He was allowed to serve his time at home wearing a tag instead of going to jail.
The new case centres on a Libyan businessman, Ziad Takieddine, who had said he had written proof that Sarkozy's 2007 campaign bid was "abundantly" financed by Tripoli, and that the €50m (£43m) in payments continued after he became president.
Takieddine, who died last year, withdrew his accusations in an interview in 2020.
At the time, Sarkozy was said to have stated: the "truth is finally coming out", but officials found the retraction to be "insincere" and a new investigation was launched into the "Save Sarko" file – the nickname the alleged perpetrators had used for the operation, according to French media.
So the former head of state and his wife, an Italian-born former supermodel and singer, will now face the charge of "criminal conspiracy with intent to commit fraud" as well as benefiting from witness tampering. They deny any wrongdoing.

The explosion ripped through one of the city's central squares
A car bomb has exploded in the central Colombian city of Villavicencio, injuring at least 23 people.
The explosive device was detonated in front of the offices of the regional government, in the city centre, damaging several buildings.
No group has so far admitted carrying out the attack - the latest in a series using explosives to target official buildings and security forces' headquarters.
Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella blamed "narcoterrorism", but gave no details. Armed criminal groups have recently stepped up attacks in what appears to be retaliation for an offensive ordered against them by De la Espriella.
Writing on social media, the president said that his government would "bluntly and forcefully" respond , external to "every drop of Colombian blood spilled".
It is the latest in a series of attacks targeting official buildings and security forces' headquarters
Three weeks ago, three adults and a baby were killed in a car bomb attack near army barracks in Tolima province .
And earlier on Monday, drones dropped explosives on the police headquarters in the northern city of Cúcuta.
The car bomb in Villavicencio went off on Monday evening - the eve of the 10th anniversary of the signing of a peace deal between the government and left-wing rebels of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (Farc), Colombia's largest guerrilla group.
Following the signing of the deal, thousands of left-wing rebel fighters laid down their arms.
However, a significant number of Farc members, who did not agree with the deal, refused to disarm and joined dissident groups instead.
While forced displacement, child recruitment and the numbers of attacks on security forces dropped in the aftermath of the deal, there has been an upsurge in recent years driven by dissident Farc factions and criminal groups fighting for control of drug trafficking, illegal mining and extortion rackets.
Colombia's first left-wing president, who was in power from August 2022 to August 2026, tried to negotiate with these armed groups as part of what he called his "total peace" strategy.
However, the talks stalled and collapsed with several of the criminal groups violating ceasefires they had agreed to observe.
De la Espriella was elected on a promise to crack down on "narcoterrorism" and has been scathing about his predecessor's approach.
He has also been critical of the 2016 agreement, calling it a "false peace".
In a post on X, uploaded shortly before news of the car bomb in Villavicencio spread, he referred to the peace deal as a "mess", describing it as a "waste of public resources" and the "cause behind Colombia's ruin".
Former President Juan Manuel Santos and Rodrigo Londoño - the two men who signed the peace deal on behalf of the Colombian government and the Farc respectively - defended it in an interview with BBC Mundo ahead of the anniversary .
Santos said that De la Espriella was "totally wrong" to call it a "false peace".
"He wants to use, or has bought into that cynical and mistaken theory that the violence we see today is the result of the peace deal, when the exact opposite is the case," Santos said, arguing that the problem lies with the lack of implementation of the agreement.

A hack of Russia's federal statistics agency Rosstat has revealed that at least 490,000 Russian military personnel have been killed in Ukraine since the start of Moscow's full-scale invasion in February 2022, according to data obtained by hackers and analysed by multiple independent news outlets.
Two hacking groups, Cyber Partisans of Belarus and Silent Crow — which also carried out a 2025 attack on Aeroflot's servers — extracted the data in a breach on the night of 1 November.
The hackers accessed Rosstat's electronic document management system and database, which contains around 23 terabytes of statistical, economic and personal data, including census materials.
The figure of at least 490,000 deaths derives from official death certificates registered between February 2022 and the end of August 2026.
Meduza, applying actuarial and epidemiological modelling to the data, estimated at least 720,000 irrecoverable losses when it includes those missing in action. Rosstat's documents alone cannot capture the full toll, as the database does not include servicemen whose deaths have not yet been registered.
Researchers and journalists justify including the missing in total loss figures because, according to Mediazona, confirmed survival is recorded in fewer than 10% of missing servicemen cases.
Under current battlefield conditions, with drone warfare making the evacuation of bodies increasingly difficult, the death tally is likely to grow.
Deaths are also registered with an average delay of 3.5 months, and those of missing soldiers with a delay of about a year, Novaya Evropa reported.
Using the conservative estimate of 490,000 to 500,000 dead, Russia sustained an average of 280 to 300 fatalities a day — one death every five minutes — according to Important Stories, which examined the leak alongside more than a dozen other independent outlets.
The outlet found that 92% of Russian servicemen died from explosions and shrapnel, with firearms accounting for only 1.3% of deaths. The Insider identified more than 370,000 of the dead by name.
The BBC Russian Service and Mediazona said at least 7,421 foreigners have been killed fighting on Russia's side.
Journalists also analysed deaths among Russian servicemen from non-combat causes. Around 2,500 died as a result of alcohol and drug use or suicide.
According to confidential Rosstat data analysed by the international news outlets, more than 1,000 Russian servicemen took their own lives since the start of the invasion.
The deaths of another 885 soldiers in Ukraine or near its borders were registered as firearm injuries "with undetermined intent," a classification experts believe is used in some cases to conceal suicides.
Together, the two figures represent a number comparable to a full Russian regiment.
Military analysts note the problem is deepened in the Russian armed forces by intense pressure from fellow soldiers and commanders, fear of assignment to high-casualty fighting areas known as "meatgrinder assaults," and contracts that in practice prevent soldiers from leaving the war.
The number of Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine is the highest in Russia's Far East and Siberia relative to their populations.
Russia's Jewish Autonomous Region in the Far East recorded nearly 1,000 deaths per 100,000 inhabitants, Zabaykalsky around 800, Chukotka 760 and Tuva 650.
Moscow, which the authorities have worked to insulate from the visible effects of the war, recorded 63 deaths per 100,000 inhabitants, according to Important Stories.
The Kremlin does not publish or recognise figures for Russian losses from the invasion. Russian authorities have restricted access to official databases and prosecuted those conducting independent counts.
Ukraine's General Staff estimated Russia's losses since February 2022 at 1,639,641 servicemen, encompassing both killed and wounded, although the figure has not been independently verified.
The Economist, in a study published at the end of October, put the number of Russian servicemen killed at between 374,000 and 770,000, and total losses including the wounded at between 1.4 and 2.1 million.
The Ukrainian armed forces' General Staff reported that October of this year was the bloodiest month for Russia since the invasion began.
The Insider said the Russian armed forces suffered their heaviest losses in spring 2025, during fighting on the Pokrovsk axis, when more than 61,000 were killed over three months.

Landmine monitor found 84 percent of deaths caused by landmines were in Southeast Asia.
Casualties from landmines or unexploded ordnance reached a five-year high in 2025, with the largest number of deaths recorded in Southeast Asia, largely driven by Myanmar’s civil war.
A report by the International Campaign to Ban Landmines found civilians were the most affected, making up some 84 percent of the 6,929 casualties recorded in 2025, half of them were children.
In Myanmar, where both the government and armed groups are using landmines, 1,891 deaths were recorded in 2025, the highest number of any country for the third consecutive year.
On average, five people are killed or wounded by landmines daily in Myanmar, the report found.
“Myanmar has gone beyond crisis to catastrophe, and has claimed the ignoble title of top producer of landmine victims for a third year in a row,” said Yeshua Moser-Puangsuwan, a co-author of the Landmine Monitor 2026 report.
“There is now contamination at some level in almost two-thirds of the townships of the country.”
Myanmar – along with Cambodia, Laos, Vietnam and other countries in the region – accounted for 27 percent of global deaths from landmines in 2025, despite having only 8 percent of the world’s population.
Syria saw a spike of more than 50 percent in casualties, with 1,602 deaths recorded in 2025 after large numbers of civilians returned after the fall of ousted President Bashar al-Assad in 2024.
“Syria is huge, but it is a post-war crisis,” Moser-Puangsuwan said. “People are now returning, and that is driving the casualty figure. They need to radically scale up their clearance capacity.”
The International Campaign to Ban Landmines has been urging more countries to join the 1997 Mine Ban Treaty to end stockpiling, production and the transfer of antipersonnel mines.
Despite this, five countries on the borders with Russia – Finland, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania and Poland – pulled out of the treaty, citing the “security situation in our region”.
Ukraine, meanwhile, notified the United Nations that it had decided to suspend the implementation of the treaty, even though such a move is not allowed under its provisions.
Russia, not a party to the treaty, has been making widespread use of mines in its invasion of Ukraine, and Landmine Monitor found that Ukraine had been using them as well.
Lebanon, the Marshall Islands and Tonga all joined the Mine Ban Treaty during the reporting period, and 162 countries are now bound by it.

France's former president Nicolas Sarkozy and his wife, singer Carla Bruni-Sarkozy, are set to be tried in 2027 on charges of "criminal conspiracy with intent to commit fraud" as well as benefitting from witness tampering. The new charges are related to the Sarkozy couple's actions during the case examining illegal campaign funding from Libyan strongman Muammar Gaddafi over which Sarkozy was imprisoned last year.
France 's ex-president Nicolas Sarkozy , his wife, singer Carla Bruni-Sarkozy , and a paparazzi boss will stand trial next year over alleged witness tampering in a case over funding for his 2007 election, a source close to the case said Tuesday.
France's right-wing leader from 2007 to 2012 has been embroiled in legal woes since leaving office.
Last year he became modern France's first former president to go to jail over seeking illegal campaign funding from late Libyan dictator Muammar Gaddafi in exchange for help restoring his international image.
Read more Ex-president Sarkozy’s 20-day prison diary: ‘Like the Count of Monte Cristo’?
The former head of state was freed from jail after 20 days pending his appeal, and an appeals court is to issue its ruling on Monday.
One of the main accusers in the case was French-Lebanese businessman Ziad Takieddine , who died in Lebanon last year.
In 2016 he claimed he helped deliver up to €5 million ($6 million) in cash from Gaddafi to Sarkozy and the former president's chief of staff in 2006 and 2007.
But in November 2020, Takieddine suddenly retracted his incriminating statement in an interview with French media.
Read more Key Lebanese-French accuser in Sarkozy Libya funding probe dies on eve of verdict
This prompted accusations that Sarkozy and his wife enlisted the help of paparazzi queen Mimi Marchand to pay the witness to change his mind, something they have always denied.
Bruni is suspected of having requested a clandestine phone line in late 2019 to communicate with Marchand about the Takieddine operation.
A court will in November next year try Sarkozy and Bruni on charges of "criminal conspiracy with intent to commit fraud" as well as benefitting from witness tampering, the source told AFP.
Marchand stands accused of "criminal conspiracy with intent to commit fraud" as well as witness tampering.
Their lawyers did not immediately respond to an AFP request for comment.
The defendants face a maximum sentence of 10 years in prison and a fine of €150,000.
Sarkozy has received two definitive convictions in other cases – linked to overspending in his failed 2012 re-election bid, and later trying to extract favours from a judge.
Marchand was last year handed an 18-month suspended prison sentence for blackmailing a television host, who feared the paparazzi boss would publish images of her daughter leaving police custody.

Öte yandan Kobra Murat, yalnızca bir hafta önce sağlık sorunlarını anlatmıştı. 'Çok kötüyüm yavrum. 13 tane ameliyatlıyım, çok yoruluyorum' diyen Murat, sevenlerinden dua istemiş, torununun evlendiğini görmek istediğini söylemişti. Sanatçı, Aralık 2023 'te de bağırsak çatlağı nedeniyle acil ameliyata alınmıştı.
Eylül ayında ise yabancı numaralardan tehdit mesajları aldığını, kendisinden 1 milyon dolar istendiğini açıklayarak suç duyurusunda bulunmuştu. Zorlu geçen ayların ardından Kobra Murat'ın yüzü bu kez oğlunun nişanıyla güldü.

Chen is the fourth Politburo member to be probed since last year in a campaign that has targeted top Chinese leaders.
China’s anticorruption watchdog has launched an investigation into the top Chinese Communist Party leader in Shanghai and member of the elite Politburo, Chen Jining, according to state media.
The 62-year-old, who is the fourth member of the top leadership body to be probed since last year, is suspected of “severe violations of discipline and laws”, the Xinhua news agency reported. The phrase is a common euphemism for corruption.
As part of President Xi Jinping’s widening anticorruption campaign , three Politburo members from the 24-member body have already been removed in its current term, which began in 2022, including General Zhang Youxia and He Weidong, both senior members of the Central Military Commission that oversees the armed forces, and Ma Xingrui, a provincial party secretary.
Mingda Qiu, a senior analyst at the Eurasia Group, said Chen’s investigation was part of an “unprecedented pattern”.
“The takedown again shows that Xi Jinping’s anticorruption campaign has no limits,” he said.
Chen earned a doctorate in environmental engineering at Imperial College London and rose through the ranks at China’s elite Tsinghua University to become its president.
He entered government as China’s environmental protection minister before becoming the mayor of Beijing. In 2022, he joined the Politburo as the party boss of Shanghai, China’s financial hub.
The post is one of China’s most prestigious provincial-level positions, often serving as a springboard to top leadership roles. Xi briefly served in the role in 2007 before joining the Politburo’s Standing Committee, the country’s highest decision-making body.
China’s second-ranking official, Prime Minister Li Qiang, as well as Vice President Han Zheng, also held the Shanghai post before moving into central leadership roles.
In a separate development, Liu Min, a senior official at the Ministry of Science and Technology, has also been placed under investigation for suspected “serious violations of party discipline and national laws”.

Irish presidency of EU proposes giving UK ‘partner’ status on assembly of cars in possible boost to reset of relations
The UK would not have to follow the EU and apply tariffs on Chinese car imports under an Irish proposal that could prove another breakthrough for the prime minister, Andy Burnham, in his reset of relations with the bloc.
The proposal comes as the UK’s foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, told a parliamentary committee that there had been “a transformation in the EU view”.
Ireland, which holds the rotating EU presidency and plays a central role in steering legislation, has come up with a compromise under which the UK would be included in the bloc’s new “Made in Europe” legislation without having to align with the EU’s trade policies.
Made in Europe , or the Industrial Accelerator Act (IAA), is designed to protect the bloc’s supply chains from cheap competition, mainly from China, particularly in the automotive and clean energy sectors.
It is understood that in a fourth compromise text, due to be considered by EU competition ministers on 3 December, Ireland has proposed giving the European Economic Area, Switzerland and the UK “partner” status for the assembly of cars.
This would allow not only cars such as the Mini, made at BMW’s Oxford factory, to qualify as European, but also vehicles made by the Japanese firm Nissan at its vast Sunderland plant .
Under the compromise, a “partner” country would agree to mutual access to any subsidies available to EU-owned assembly plants, and to public procurement contracts for fleet cars.
Miliband said he thought the EU had considerably changed its view on UK inclusion since Burnham became PM.
“My sense is that view has been transformed and that is somewhat reflected in the agreement.
“I think we are heading for a good outcome on Made in Europe and I think there is a real understanding and we should also thank our our allies who argued for us to be in Made in Europe not outside,” he said.
Irish negotiators have also suggested giving Japan and South Korea, which lobbied hard against the original Made in Europe proposals, access to public procurement and other public support schemes for car parts and components.
A spokesperson for the Irish presidency said: “Having listened closely to all member states, the presidency has proposed a pragmatic and balanced way forward on the IAA to deliver for European competitiveness.”
Burnham last week took the biggest step towards deeper ties with the EU since Brexit, sealing deals to ease trade and create a mobility scheme for young people.
The latest iteration of the IAA text is designed to reflect the car sector’s position as a cornerstone of European industry.
France, which championed the legislation, originally opposed the inclusion of the UK at all but dropped its opposition last month on condition that the UK dynamically align with the EU on tariffs on Chinese vehicles.
But this caused further tensions with the UK . The business secretary, Jonathan Reynolds, insisted the British government would not be coerced into imposing tariffs on Chinese vehicles and would only take steps that were in the national interest.
Mike Hawes, the chief executive of the Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders, said the UK “should not become collateral damage” from measures intended to address concerns arising elsewhere in the global market.
The UK car industry has argued that it is so intertwined with its EU counterparts that both sides would be damaged if the UK was not included in Made in Europe.
Hawes said: “It is essential that the final arrangements recognise the unique UK-EU automotive relationship as allies in adversity, and do not create new barriers to our shared supply chains.”
The latest proposal will be discussed by an EU working group involving industry leaders and EU member states on Friday, before being finessed further for consideration by ministers.
European carmakers are attempting to respond to a flood of cheap Chinese electric vehicles into the bloc. ⁠Volkswagen began wage talks ⁠with labour representatives on ​Tuesday amid mounting worker anger over deep cost cuts , with protesters carrying black coffins to symbolise what they said was the death of trust and the company’s future prospects.
China faces further restrictions on its trade with EU: tariffs were imposed on Chinese EV imports in 2024, and quotas agreed with Beijing in October come into force on 1 December.
The Chinese electric vehicle maker BYD ⁠said on ⁠Tuesday that it had entered into exclusive ⁠negotiations with the billionaire Jim Ratcliffe’s Ineos Automotive to buy ⁠its manufacturing plant in ‌Hambach, France, ‌as it seeks ‌more European production ahead of Made in Europe legislation expected next year.
Separately, Ineos said on Tuesday it would begin production of its Grenadier 4x4 in the US in 2028.

Dünyanın farklı ülkelerinden oyuncular, televizyon dünyasının tanınmış isimleri ve sektör temsilcilerinin katıldığı törenin sunuculuğunu Michael Urie yaptı.

Gecede 22 ülkeden 64 aday arasından 16 kategoride kazananlar açıklandı. Birleşik Krallık dokuz ödülle en çok ödülü kazanan ülke oldu.

Eski Fransa Cumhurbaşkanı Nicolas Sarkozy ve eşi Carla Bruni-Sarkozy, ‘suç işlemek amacıyla örgüt kurmak’ suçundan 2027’de yargılanacak.
2007-2012 dönemi Fransa cumhurbaşkanı Sarkozy, 2007’de cumhurbaşkanı seçim kampanyasını yürütmek için dönemin Libya lideri Muammer Kaddafi’den yasadışı maddi destek almakla suçlanıyordu.
Fransız-Lübnan kökenli Takieddine’nin de 2006 sonlarında Libya’dan Sarkozy’ye beş milyon avro getirdiği iddia edilmişti.
İddiaların ardından 2013’te olayla ilgili soruşturma açılmış, böylece ‘Libya davası’ denilen yargı süreci başlamıştı. Sarkozy bu dava sonunda 21 Ekim-10 Kasım 2025 tarihlerinde La Santé hapishanesinde tutuklu kalmıştı.
Yerel basındaki haberlere göre Paris’teki soruşturma hakimleri, Sarkozy ve eşi Bruni-Sarkozy’nin de aralarında olduğu 11 kişinin gelecek yıl mahkemeye çıkmasına karar verdi.
Sarkozy ve eşi Bruni-Sarkozy, 3 Kasım-2 Aralık 2027’da ‘suç işlemek amacıyla örgüt kurmak’ ve ‘tanığı manipüle etme’ suçlarından yargılanacak.
Soruşturma kapsamında Sarkozy’nin, ‘kilit tanık’ statüsündeki Takieddine’in kendisi hakkındaki ifadesini değiştirmesi için 2020’de hukuk dışı yöntemlere başvurup başvurmadığı araştırılıyordu.
Öte yandan Sarkozy’nin yargılandığı ‘Libya davası’ na ilişkin temyiz kararının 30 Kasım’da çıkması bekleniyor.
İş insanı Takieddine önce Sarkozy’nin Libya’dan finansman aldığını savunmuş, sonra 2020’de ifadelerini değiştirip aksini iddia etmişti.
Sarkozy’nin suçlamaları çekmesi için Takieddine’ye farklı kişiler aracılığıyla baskı yapıp yapmadığı soruşturuluyor.
75 yaşındaki Takieddine, 23 Eylül 2025’te Lübnan’ın başkenti Beyrut’ta ölmüştü.
Paris Ceza Mahkemesi, 25 Eylül 2025’te görülen ‘Libya davası’ nda, Sarkozy’nin ‘pasif yolsuzluk, kamu fonlarını zimmete geçirmeyi gizleme ve yasa dışı kampanya finansmanı’ suçlarından beraatine, ‘suç örgütü kurmak’ suçundansa beş yıl hapis cezasına çarptırılmasına karar vermişti.
Sarkozy, karara itiraz etse de mahkeme kararının niteliği gereği temyiz süreci sonuçlanmadan hapse girmesi kesinleşmişti.
Fransa’da 21 Ekim 2025’te cezaevine giren Sarkozy, 20 gün sonra adli kontrol şartıyla serbest bırakılmıştı.
Sarkozy, 20 gün süren hapis hayatını ‘Bir Mahkumun Günlüğü’ adıyla kitaplaştırmıştı :
“Hapiste ne görülecek ne de yapılacak bir şey var. La Santé’de sessizliği unuttum; duyulacak çok şey var ve ne yazık ki sürekli gürültü… Tıpkı çöl gibi, hapiste içsel yaşam güçleniyor.”
Sarkozy, Fransa tarihinde İkinci Dünya Savaşı’nın ardından hapse atılan Nazi işbirlikçisi Philippe Pétain’dan sonra tutuklanan ilk cumhurbaşkanı olmuştu.

Bestesi Güldiyar Tanrıdağlı’ya, librettosu Prof. Dr. İskender Pala’ya ait eser; Lidya Krallığı’nın son döneminde yaşanan siyasi mücadeleleri, Pers tehdidini ve insan ilişkilerini müziğin anlatım gücüyle izleyiciye aktaracak.
MÖ 6. yüzyılda ekonomik zenginliği, siyasi gücü ve başkenti Sard ile Anadolu tarihinin önemli uygarlıklarından biri olan Lidya Krallığı ’nın son dönemini konu alan eser, tarihsel olayları evrensel değerler üzerinden ele alıyor.
Bir toplumun gerçek gücünün sahip olduğu topraklardan, zenginliklerden ve siyasi iktidardan çok, kuşaktan kuşağa aktardığı kültürel miras ve değerlerde saklı olduğu düşüncesinden hareket eden opera; adalet, toplumsal düzen ve etik değerler üzerinden uygarlıkların kalıcılığını sorguluyor.
Rejisör Caner Akın tarafından sahneye konulan eser, geleneksel opera anlatımını çağdaş ve deneysel sahneleme teknikleriyle buluşturuyor.
Dekor, kostüm, ışık ve video tasarımlarıyla zenginleşen prodüksiyon, Lidya’nın tarihsel dünyasını günümüz sahnesine taşırken izleyicilere görsel ve müzikal bir deneyim sunuyor.
İstanbul Devlet Opera ve Balesi Orkestrasını İbrahim Yazıcı’nın yöneteceği prodüksiyonun dekor ve görsel tasarımını Efter Tunç, kostüm tasarımını Olcay Engin Kaymaz, ışık tasarımını Cem Yılmazer, video tasarımını Aisha Hajiyeva, koreografisini ise Berk Sarıbay üstleniyor. İstanbul Devlet Opera ve Balesi Korosu’nu Anıl Aydın hazırlıyor.
Eserde Edusa karakterini dönüşümlü olarak Gülbin Günay ve Evren Işık Yasemin canlandıracak. Halludas rolünde Mert Süngü ve Ufuk Toker, Krezüs rolünde Göktuğ Alpaşar ve Gökhan Ürben, Namirek rolünde Nesrin Gönüldağ ve Asude Karayavuz, Kyros rolünde Yoel Keşap ve Hüseyin Likos, Solon rolünde Caner Akgün ve Kevork Tavityan, Karuna rolünde Barbora Hitay ve Deniz Likos sahne alacak.
Eserin geniş sanatçı kadrosunda Berk Dalkılıç, Bülent Külekçi, Alper Göçeri, Murat Güney, Kenan Dağaşan, Emre Güngör, Burak Kul, Talip Savranbaşı, Arda Durgut, Ufuk Karakoç, Efe Doğrukul, Bahadır Özkoca, Uğur Etiler, Okan Fidan, Mehmet Tükel Acar, Fuat Kılıç Aslan ve Mehmet Eminhan Turgut’un yanı sıra İstanbul Devlet Opera ve Balesi bale ve modern dans sanatçıları da yer alacak.
Geçtiğimiz sezon dünya prömiyeri gerçekleştirilen ve İstanbul Devlet Opera ve Balesi repertuvarında yerini alan “Edusa”, 26 ve 28 Kasım ile 10 ve 12 Aralık 2026 tarihlerinde Atatürk Kültür Merkezi Türk Telekom Opera Salonu’nda sanatseverlerle buluşacak.
